headline: 高盛把 Claude Code 从银行家和交易员手里收回，说明企业级 AI 编程的第一道坎不是能力而是可控性

overview_bullets.text: 高盛撤下 Claude Code，与同日苹果 CEO 施压软件负责人加码 AI 形成对照：大厂对 AI 的态度正从“全员铺开”转向“先管住风险再谈规模”。
今日多篇论文指向同一件事——不更新模型权重、只改 agent harness 也能带来递归自我改进，智能体的竞争重心正从模型转向脚手架。
284B 的 DeepSeek 被塞进 64GB 内存无 GPU 运行，加上 4 卡 R9700 的实测吞吐，本地大模型正从玩具变成可用的生产力配置。
agent memory 呼唤 OpenTelemetry 式标准、billion-context 做 5 倍 token 压缩，说明长会话的瓶颈已从窗口大小转为可观测与成本。
“我不用 LLM 写代码”“对抗 AI 脑疲劳”“把 AI 生成的 PR 描述藏起来”同时上榜，一线开发者对 AI 编码的疲劳感正在公开化。

executive_summary: 今天最清晰的信号是：AI 的瓶颈正从模型能力迁移到组织可控性、上下文工程与开发者耐受度，谁能把这三件事工程化，谁才拿得下企业订单。

editor_note.core: 🎯 高盛撤下 Claude Code 是今天最该记住的一件事：它证明企业采用 AI 编程的分水岭不在模型能不能写代码，而在合规、审计与责任归属能不能兜住，一旦兜不住，采购规模再大也会被一键回收。
editor_note.cross_signal: 🔍 论文侧说 harness 演化能在不改权重的前提下持续提升智能体表现，开源侧同一天冒出 agent-browser、anthropics/skills、billion-context 这些脚手架与上下文工具——研究判断与工程供给在同一天对齐，说明“外壳层”已是真实赛道。
editor_note.counterintuitive: 🔄 热度最高的 sherlock（92.1）只是一个社工用户名检索工具，与 AI 无关；而真正决定企业能否落地的 agent memory 标准化只拿到 58.9，热度与价值明显错位。
editor_note.risk: ⚠️ 最大的盲点是“基准分数幻觉”：harness 论文自己就在质疑更高 benchmark 是否等于可靠、可迁移的提升，而企业正拿这些分数做采购决策，一旦真实任务掉链子，退潮会比高盛这次更剧烈。

contradictions: 高盛从银行家和交易员手中收回 Claude Code，与苹果 CEO 施压软件负责人推进更激进 AI 战略，同为大厂却给出相反信号。
“AI 泡沫不存在”的辩护与“药企 CEO 不买 AI 治病的账”并列出现，资本叙事与产业买家判断背离。
一边是开发者宣称不在编码中使用 LLM，一边是大量 PR 由 Claude Code / Codex 生成、需要专门“藏起 slop 描述”，实践与表态不一致。

sections.name: 开源项目
sections.summary: 开源侧火力集中在智能体基础设施——浏览器自动化、技能库、上下文压缩与 GPU 管理面，而非又一个模型。

sections.name: 论文与研究
sections.summary: 研究主线是“不碰权重也能变强”：harness 演化、权重空间编程、模型接力协作，以及视频世界模型与流式 ASR 的工程化收敛。

sections.name: 社区舆论
sections.summary: 社区情绪分裂：一边是本地推理的硬核实测与“AI 泡沫不存在”的辩护，一边是对 AI 编码疲劳和 slop PR 的公开抵触。

sections.name: 产业与新闻
sections.summary: 产业面出现明显温差：高盛收缩、药企 CEO 不买账，而苹果与英伟达仍在加注，AI 叙事进入“兑现期”而非“宣传期”。

comments.one_liner: 一个通过用户名在多个社交网络上追踪对应账号的开源工具
comments.why: 按用户名跨平台批量定位社交账号，把公开信息聚合成一份可被任何人（包括骚扰者、招聘方、执法方）使用的画像，隐私边界被进一步压缩。
comments.stance: 工具本身中立，但默认把「可被找到」当成常态，这是对普通用户不利的默认值。

comments.one_liner: 一个开源的 Grok Bot 替代方案，内置可供 bot 使用的虚拟机
comments.why: 把虚拟机交给机器人操作，等于给自动化代理一个可执行代码、可持久化的落脚点，开源复刻让这类能力从厂商封闭产品扩散到任意开发者手中。
comments.stance: 能力扩散快于安全护栏，先跑起来再补边界是这一波代理项目的通病。

comments.one_liner: Meta 开源的可完全定制、面向 agent 的设计系统
comments.why: 设计系统明确面向 agent 就绪，意味着组件层开始为机器调用而非人类点击做接口约定，前端资产的可复用对象从人变成代理。
comments.stance: 方向对，但「agent ready」目前更像营销标签，缺少可验证的调用契约。

comments.one_liner: 上下文压缩插件 billion-context，支持月级长会话、100K 小窗口运行并节省约 5 倍 token。
comments.why: 把上下文压缩做成插件，直接攻击长会话的成本与窗口瓶颈，小窗口模型因此能承接月级任务，推理预算的分配方式被改写。
comments.stance: 压缩换来的省 token 必然以信息损失为代价，宣称省 5 倍就该公开召回率的代价。

comments.one_liner: vercel-labs 推出的浏览器自动化 CLI，供 AI agent 调用
comments.why: 把浏览器操作封装成 CLI，等于给 AI agent 一个不依赖图形界面的确定性执行层，网页抓取与流程自动化的接入成本被压到一条命令。
comments.stance: 方向正确，但浏览器自动化是权限与反爬的高危地带，谁掌握执行层谁就掌握 agent 的落地边界。

comments.one_liner: Anthropic 官方维护的 Agent Skills 公开仓库。
comments.why: 厂商亲自维护公开技能仓库，技能格式从社区约定升级为官方标准，第三方技能包将围绕它分层并接受兼容性审查。
comments.stance: 官方入场是技能生态的分水岭，但标准由单一厂商把持，长期看是锁定风险。

comments.one_liner: DeepMind 的通用物理仿真器，支持多关节动力学与接触模拟
comments.why: 通用物理仿真器是机器人学习与具身智能的底座，持续活跃意味着训练环境与真实硬件之间的迁移成本在下降。
comments.stance: 这类基础设施比任何单个模型发布都更能决定具身智能的落地速度。

comments.one_liner: Anthropic 官方示例项目集，帮助开发者用 Claude API 快速搭建可部署应用
comments.why: 官方给出可直接部署的起步项目，把开发者从「读文档试错」拉到「改模板上线」，缩短了从 API 到产品的路径，也把生态锁定提前到第一行代码。
comments.stance: 降低门槛的同时在培养路径依赖，这是标准的平台圈地动作。

comments.one_liner: 面向裸金属 GPU Kubernetes 的管理平面 NVKE
comments.why: 裸金属上的 GPU Kubernetes 管理面，瞄准的是自建算力集群的调度与隔离问题，直接冲击云厂商在 GPU 资源上的溢价空间。
comments.stance: 自建 GPU 集群的门槛正在被这类管理面拉低，云厂商的算力租金会被压缩。

comments.one_liner: 一篇考察 agent harness 演进能否在不更新模型权重的情况下实现递归自我改进的论文
comments.why: 论文把「不改权重、只改代理外壳」当作递归自我改进的路径，并追问基准分数是否等于可迁移能力，直接质疑当前代理评测的可信度。
comments.stance: 分数上涨不等于能力上涨，这篇的价值在于给代理热潮泼冷水。

comments.one_liner: 一项让生成式视频模型推演视野之外世界演化的研究 EvoWorld
comments.why: 视频生成模型被当作世界模拟器使用，但渲染逼真与推演世界演化是两种能力，论文把这一错位摆上台面，影响所有拿视频模型做规划的人。
comments.stance: 把生成模型当世界模型是当前最被高估的类比，需要更多这类拆解。

comments.one_liner: 一项用 agentic coding 强化视频生成可控性的工作 Video-Coder
comments.why: 用代理式编码强化视频生成的空间结构与可控性，把「写代码」变成视频生成的控制通道，改变的是创作者对生成结果的干预粒度。
comments.stance: 用代码换可控性是正确取舍，但代价是创作门槛从提示词转向编程能力。

comments.one_liner: 一个面向实时转写、采用稳定前缀的流式 ASR 模型 Confucius4-R2T2
comments.why: 流式识别的主要消费者变成翻译器与语音代理，被后续修正的 token 会造成重复劳动或错误动作，稳定前缀直接决定下游系统的可靠性。
comments.stance: 实时转写的竞争点已从准确率转向「不反悔」，这是被低估的工程指标。

comments.one_liner: 一篇系统评估 Weight-Space Programming（WSP）的论文，考察推理 agent 直接读写神经网络参数的能力边界、跨任务泛化与局限。
comments.why: 把「改权重」当成智能体的可编程接口，等于绕开梯度训练直接编辑模型行为，一旦泛化性被验证，微调与适配器生态的护城河会被削薄。
comments.stance: 方向诱人，但论文自认局限未明，现在谈替代训练为时过早。

comments.one_liner: AgentBaton：一种在长程 agent 任务中让云端强模型与本地高效模型协作分工的调度方案。
comments.why: 让便宜小模型跑常规步骤、只在卡壳时调用云端强模型，直接把长程任务的 token 成本压下来，云厂商按调用量收钱的商业模式首当其冲。
comments.stance: 这是智能体落地真正缺的那块拼图，省钱比刷榜更有价值。

comments.one_liner: KetchUp：用 Rust 和 WebGPU 构建的开源 SketchUp 替代品。
comments.why: 用 Rust 加 WebGPU 在浏览器里重做建模工具，把原本绑定桌面与授权费的 CAD 工作流搬到零安装的网页端，专业软件的许可壁垒被从底层绕过。
comments.stance: 开源替代品赢不了功能，但能赢掉「先装个软件」这道门槛。

comments.one_liner: Llama-modchip：在 64GB 内存、无 GPU 的机器上运行 284B 规模 DeepSeek 模型的项目。
comments.why: 把超大模型塞进 64GB 内存靠的是量化与内存换显存，意味着高端推理的硬件门槛从显卡转向内存条，个人工作站重新具备跑大模型的能力。
comments.stance: 速度不会好看，但「没有 GPU 也能跑」这件事本身就在改写采购逻辑。

comments.one_liner: 一篇作者分享自己如何应对 AI 信息过载与注意力疲劳的随笔。
comments.why: 当工程师开始把对抗 AI 疲劳当成日常课题，说明工具带来的认知负荷已经反噬产出，团队评估 AI 工具时得把注意力成本算进账。
comments.stance: 把疲劳当个人修养问题谈是逃避，这是工具设计和工作节奏的问题。

comments.one_liner: 一篇主张 agent 记忆领域需要类似 OpenTelemetry 的统一可观测性标准的文章。
comments.why: 智能体的记忆目前各家自造格式、无法跨框架迁移与观测，缺一套统一遥测标准就意味着换框架等于记忆清零，锁定效应由此产生。
comments.stance: 呼吁得对，但标准从来是赢家写的，先看谁愿意放弃私有格式。

comments.one_liner: 一位开发者撰文说明自己为何在编码工作中拒绝使用 LLM。
comments.why: 一线开发者公开拒绝在编码中用 LLM，暴露的是代码审查、责任归属与长期可维护性的真实成本，而不只是效率之争。
comments.stance: 拒绝是合理选择，但把它讲成原则问题多半会随工具成熟而软化。

comments.one_liner: 一篇对「AI 泡沫」说法提出质疑的评论文章。
comments.why: 对泡沫论的质疑把讨论从情绪拉回现金流与算力利用率，若收入端真能跟上资本开支，估值争论的焦点会从「有没有泡沫」转向「谁在裸泳」。
comments.stance: 论点站得住一半：泡沫不在需求，在二线玩家借债堆算力的那一层。

comments.one_liner: 用户分享四卡 R9700 配置下运行 QFN 3.8 的初步基准数据，含单用户约 190 tok/s 的生成速度与 prefill 表现。
comments.why: 多卡消费级显卡跑出近 190 tok/s 与稳定预填充，说明本地推理的吞吐已能支撑多人并发，小团队自建推理服务开始比按 token 付费更划算。
comments.stance: 这类实测比任何发布会都更能说明本地部署的临界点到了。

comments.one_liner: Goldman Sachs 正在撤下其银行家与交易员使用的 Claude Code。
comments.why: 高盛撤下编码助手，说明金融业对代码与数据的合规审查压过了效率收益，其他受监管行业会跟着收紧内部 AI 工具的部署范围。
comments.stance: 这不是 AI 失败，是合规部门终于开始认真读条款了。

comments.one_liner: 硅谷宣称 AI 将攻克疾病，但制药公司 CEO 们对此持怀疑态度
comments.why: 制药业掌握临床验证与监管通道，其 CEO 的冷淡态度决定 AI 药物发现能否从融资叙事变成可上市管线，直接影响一批 AI 生物公司的估值逻辑。
comments.stance: 怀疑是对的：没有湿实验与临床数据，硅谷的治愈承诺只是把失败风险转嫁给患者。

comments.one_liner: Apple CEO 施压软件负责人，要求其推进更具野心的 AI 战略
comments.why: CEO 直接向软件负责人施压，意味着苹果把 AI 从功能补丁提升为组织级优先级，将改变其内部资源分配与对外合作节奏。
comments.stance: 苹果的问题不是野心不够，而是隐私架构与端侧算力自我设限，换人施压解决不了。

comments.one_liner: 一位开发者讲述如何把 Claude Code、Codex 生成的 PR 描述藏起来，并分享以 PR 为工作单元的开发流程
comments.why: 当 PR 由代理生成，评审者面对的是缺乏意图说明的变更包，审查成本从写代码转移到重建上下文，团队协作规范被迫重写。
comments.stance: 把生成式 PR 描述藏起来是掩耳盗铃，该被要求交代动机的是提交者，不是读者。

comments.one_liner: 对比用 C 和 Rust 编写 SQLite 扩展 parse_number() 的实践，该函数可将「-$1,234.56」「12.5%」等字符串转为数值
comments.why: 同一功能用 C 与 Rust 各写一遍，把扩展开发的内存安全代价与工具链摩擦量化，为 SQLite 生态选型提供可复用的对照。
comments.stance: 这类小规模双语对照比任何语言布道都有说服力，Rust 的收益必须用代码量换。

comments.one_liner: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 致员工的内部备忘录全文
comments.why: 内部备忘录全文外流，暴露英伟达对主权算力订单的争夺方式，日本采购 Rubin 芯片的规模说明国家级买家正成为其增长支柱。
comments.stance: 主权 AI 采购把芯片变成外交筹码，客户越集中，英伟达的议价权越像基础设施垄断。

comments.one_liner: AI Engineer 频道百万订阅特别节目，Mihail Eric 谈 Stanford 如何教授 AI 原生工程
comments.why: 课程设计者要回答代理能一次做完作业后该考什么，其答案会外溢成企业招聘与培训的评估标准。
comments.stance: 把开源维护者请进课堂是正确方向，真实评审比任何自动评分都难被代理糊弄。

comments.one_liner: Stanford CS146S 课程第二次开设的做法：引入开源维护者，让学生读懂陌生仓库、提出改动并向维护者解释补丁
comments.why: 让学生读陌生仓库、提改动并向可能合并的人解释补丁，考核点从写代码转向说服与责任归属，这是代理时代少数无法被提示词替代的能力。
comments.stance: 这才是 AI 原生工程教育的核心：教人承担合并后果，而不是教人调模型。

it_b575796d94556692.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
it_b575796d94556692.summary: Agent harness evolution enables recursive self-improvement (RSI) without updating model weights. We examine whether higher benchmark scores yield reliable, efficient, and transferable improvement. We evaluate four methods across harnesses, general and coding tasks. Repeated evaluations, controlled agent expansion, component interventions, and admission replays reveal recurring patterns. All sixteen evolved agents gain previously uncovered tasks while losing previously covered ones. In one general-task case, reliability rises by 5.2 points despite losing ten previously covered tasks. Most reliability gains also increase deployment cost. Specific changes usually outperform generic reminders, but their benefits can change when combined. The highest-scoring agent does not yield the largest mean improvement in any of our four pools, and stricter admission can discard useful alternatives. Transfer selectively preserves gains: coverage usually falls on the general-task target across both harness types and paradigms, but rises on the coding target with the outer-layer-only harness. These findings motivate preservation-aware evaluation, tested decision rules, and explicit applicability conditions. As a constructive follow-up, EvoAudit turns these diagnostics into revisions of select, analyze, mutate, and gate, achieving the best performance.

it_57404866eadfaf5b.title: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models
it_57404866eadfaf5b.summary: Generative video models are increasingly used as visual world simulators, yet their primary strength lies in rendering plausible pixels rather than reasoning about how a world should evolve. Coherent world evolution requires more than visual fidelity: when an event occurs, a model must infer its consequences for the entities in the world and then render the resulting state. For example, after a wild beast appears, the model should not only depict the wild beast, but also infer whether a nearby person should flee, take cover, or fight back based on the realized scene. Existing diffusion-based video models lack an explicit mechanism for maintaining world state and reasoning over such event-conditioned consequences, often producing visually plausible but behaviorally static or causally inconsistent outputs. To make this reasoning gap concrete and measurable, we propose a new problem, Out-of-Sight Causal Evolution, which requires a model to render an event, reason about its consequences for the evolving world state, and reveal a causally plausible outcome as the world continues to evolve, even out of sight. As a baseline reference solution, we introduce EvoWorld, a brain-renderer collaboration framework in which a vision-language model serves as the world brain: it observes generated segments, maintains an evolving account of the world, and reasons about plausible state transitions, while a segment-autoregressive video renderer realizes them visually. We further introduce EvoWorld-Data and EvoWorld-Bench for training and evaluating event realization, causal reactions, and revisit consistency. Experiments show that EvoWorld substantially improves event-conditioned causal evolution over recent models while preserving visual quality and consistency, establishing a reference point for reasoning-guided, autonomous world evolution beyond the current field of view.

it_29ba332ac7d8c222.summary: Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in video generation in terms of visual quality and temporal consistency. However, generating videos with precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition remains challenging. We then train Video-Coder with SFT fol- lowed by harness-native agentic reinforcement learning with dual reward feedback, which combines execution-based and video-based rewards. Additionally, we design an annealing training strategy that gradually reduces the execution reward over time, allowing the model to rely more on the video reward in the later training stages. Experiments show that Video-Coder achieves significant gains, improving Minimax-H3 by approximately 7 points on PhyGenBench and 24 points on VBench-2.0. it_63c66f140a7c9358.title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription
it_63c66f140a7c9358.summary: Streaming speech recognition is increasingly consumed by machines, such as translators and voice agents, that act on each token as it appears. A token that is later revised costs wasted work or a wrong action. In this work, we present Confucius4-R2T2 (short for Real Real-Time Transcription), a stable-prefix streaming ASR model that never modifies its earlier output while maintaining high accuracy and low latency. R2T2 is obtained by post-training Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio while freezing its pre-trained audio encoder and projector. The adaptation is based on the concept of Longest Stable Prefix (LSP), a new notion that we introduce in this work. We prove that LSP is monotone under the prefix order, consistent with the full-audio output, and maximal among labels that equal a whole earlier output. Learning from LSP labels converts a full-context model into a stable-prefix streaming one without any architectural change. Extensive evaluations show that R2T2 brings streaming recognition close to the base model's full-context quality while delivering stable text with low emission lag. Its gains extend beyond the post-training languages, demonstrating a practical path from full-context ASR to stable streaming. We open-source the model weights and code at https://huggingface.co/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2 and https://github.com/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2.

it_4b7560f88b6841e2.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
it_4b7560f88b6841e2.summary:
Weight-Space Programming (WSP) enables reasoning agents to directly inspect and modify neural network parameters, offering an alternative to gradient-based model adaptation. However, its capabilities, cross-task generalization, and practical limitations remain insufficiently understood. We systematically investigate WSP through 16 editing trajectories across seven benchmarks and two model scales (Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-9B). Our findings reveal three key insights. First, WSP can achieve substantial performance gains through highly localized interventions. On full held-out evaluations, accuracy improves by up to 29.45, 4.42, 36.72, and 17.11 percentage points on MATH-500, GPQA Diamond, IFEval, and SciBench, respectively. Notably, modifying only 1,023 parameters yields a 29.45-point improvement. Second, WSP exhibits promising but uneven cross-task generalization. A Math-edited checkpoint improves GPQA Diamond, IFEval, and SciBench by 3.03, 12.18, and 20.10 points, respectively, without further editing, while leaving SciCode performance unchanged. Third, effective editing remains challenging and inconsistent. Outcomes vary substantially across trajectories, and six of the 16 trajectories retain the original weights when candidate improvements cannot be reliably validated. Together, these results highlight WSP's potential for highly localized model adaptation while revealing important challenges in intervention discovery, reliability, and cross-task transfer.

it_5cc1694168177d2d.title: AgentBaton: Efficient Model Collaboration in Agentic Tasks
it_5cc1694168177d2d.summary: Solving long-horizon agentic tasks requires language agents to interact with their environments over multiple steps, and reliable performance often comes from the expensive capable models available through cloud providers. Meanwhile, alternative efficient models with inferior performance but a much lower cost are emerging, including lower-tier cloud models and smaller open-weights models deployable on local hardware. This raises a natural question that remains less explored than traditional query-level routing: can capable and efficient models collaborate within a single long-horizon agentic task to substantially reduce cost while preserving task accuracy? In this paper, we systematically investigate key design choices for such collaboration through model handoffs, where one model takes over from another, focusing on handoff direction and context transfer. We find that efficient-to-capable handoffs generally underperform capable-only execution with limited or even no cost reduction, whereas capable-to-efficient handoffs at suitable stages of task progress largely preserve or even improve accuracy while substantially reducing cost. These findings suggest that a one-time, simple, well-timed handoff strategy is good enough for cost-effective agent collaboration, motivating AgentBaton, a lightweight detector that learns when to hand off from recurring patterns in task progress. Across 11 model pairs and two representative benchmarks, AgentBaton reduces API costs by 65.9% on average while largely preserving task accuracy, with accuracy gains of up to 8.8 percentage points over capable-only execution. Experiments across various reasoning-effort settings further show that AgentBaton extends the empirical accuracy-cost Pareto frontier.

it_6ee1dee33e4bfc63.title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind
it_6ee1dee33e4bfc63.summary:
Most of the changes I make to my projects these days come in the form of PRs opened for me by Claude Code or Codex. The PR is my unit of work - I use them to bundle commits together, iterating on them until a feature is complete, document decisions and then merge the finished result. Today's coding agents are great at writing PR descriptions.
They're too good at describing the work
The problem is that they are too good. An agent-written PR description is accurate and comprehensive. It describes the problem, the detailed solution, and the steps taken to verify it. That's a lot of information to absorb.
It's not necessarily slop, but it reads like slop!
It's very easy to spot an AI-written PR, and as with other forms of AI writing my instant reaction is best summarized as "I'm not reading all of that". It doesn't matter how accurate or useful the information is, I'm instantly put off by the thought that it will take me longer to read than it took the driving author to write... even when that driving author is me!
I want human editorial judgement. I want someone to have thought just long enough about the PR to give me a human-approved introduction that helps me understand, at a high level, what the PR is for and whether it deserves more of my attention.
I think I've found a low-effort way to do this that feels right.
Hide most of it in a details/summary
The HTML <details><summary> elements render as a collapsed heading (the summary) that can be expanded to view the larger piece of text. The code looks like this:
< details >
< summary > Claude Opus 5.5 </ summary >
< h2 > The hook </ h2 >
Plugins implement < code > register_agent_reference_types(datasette) </ code > ...
</ details >
When rendered, it looks like this :

Crucially, <details><summary> is supported in GitHub Markdown . You can drop those tags directly into an issue comment or PR description and GitHub will hide the details and display just the summary plus an expansion arrow.
I've started using this for my AI-generated pull requests.
The opening paragraph of my PRs will be carefully selected to act as a high-level explanation of what's going on - the shortest text a human can read that will help get them up to speed.
I'll sometimes throw in a screenshot as well, since images are often the best way to quickly illustrate a new feature.
The full agent-written essay then follows in a <details><summary> . I use the model name and often the effort level as that summary, to make it abundantly clear what is going on - "Claude Opus 5.5 Medium" for example.
My PRs don't feel nearly as sloppy now! The information is all still there, but a reader can glance at it and get the top, human-curated information without their eyes glazing over at multiple paragraphs of agent-written details.
I don't always write the introduction myself - sometimes the agent has given me what I need already, hidden away in the avalanche of other text. My promise to the reader is that the short opener will represent my human judgement as to what is definitely worth their time.
Here are some recent examples where I've used this pattern, including the opener I used:


datasette PR #3052: Redesign row page as a vertical list of fields - "The row page showed its single row as a one-row table. For wide tables, like a 46-column GitHub repos table, that scrolled far off to the right and left most of the page blank." (then a screenshot)

datasette PR #3043: Pagination bar showing which rows are on the current page - "Table pages that span more than one page now make it obvious where you are, and offer navigation at the top of the page as well as the bottom." (plus screenshot)

datasette PR #3042: Load edit-tools.js on demand via a small loader - " edit-tools.js (~220KB) was loaded on every table, row and database page, even for users who couldn't edit anything. Now only load it for users who can edit when they first interact with an edit feature (including mouse over an edit link)."

datasette-agent PR #51: register_agent_reference_types plugin hook - "Lets plugins add their own kinds of item to the # tagging in the chat composer using a new register_agent_reference_types(datasette) plugin hook." - pictured above.

llm PR #1838: Add llm openai endpoint add/list/remove/path commands - "Adds commands for managing the records in extra-openai-models.yaml , so OpenAI-compatible endpoints can be saved from the command line instead of by hand-editing YAML." - then copied --help output.

The mnemonic
I used to have trouble remembering the order of the tags - is it <details><summary> or <summary><details> ?
Here are two tricks that helped me.
First, and most obviously, the <summary> is clearly the bit where you summarize the details. That's the tag for your line of text that can be clicked to expand - the <details> element must then wrap everything else.
An even better trick is to always refer to these two tags as "details-summary".
"details-summary" is two syllables followed by three syllables. That rolls off the tongue more smoothly than the three-two punch of "summary-details".
Say "details-summary" out loud just a few times and you'll never forget the order of the tags again.
(I still wish GitHub would add a button to their Markdown editor for this - partly to save me painstakingly typing it on my mobile keyboard, and partly to help spread the word to more GitHub users that this feature exists.)

What do you assign when a coding agent can finish last year’s homework in one prompt? In the second run of Stanford’s CS146S, Mihail Eric brought open-source maintainers into the course. Students have to learn an unfamiliar repo, propose a change, and explain the patch to the person who might merge it. We invited Mihail, who teaches The Modern Software Developer at Stanford and leads AI at Monaco, to celebrate one million subscribers on the AI Engineer YouTube channel. He opens up the course syllabus and shows us which lessons survived contact with his own engineering team. Monaco built its agent workspaces, bought its code review tools, and gave an on-call agent access to Datadog and GitHub. We ask how he decides which tools his team needs to own. Stanford CS146S — The ten-week syllabus and assignments.
The Emperor Has No Clothes — Mihail builds a coding agent from scratch.

it_c0fd1a7a8e5f7ead.summary: Posted this on the r/R9700 subreddit as well, but figured I'd share my initial findings here. tl;dr - One user writes at about 190 tok/s. Prefill runs at about 6,800 tok/s total no matter how many users there are. Agent follow-ups start in 0.2 to 2.5 s and write at 80 to 225 tok/s per user, even with 8 users at 128K context each. The worst case, 8 users each sending a fresh 128K prompt at the same moment, waits about 2.5 minutes for the first token. Yes yes I know the cards aren't all matching (the perfectionist in me is annoyed but they'll be in a case so who cares). PC Specs: CPU - EPYC 7402P Motherboard - Asrock ROMED8-2T RAM - 128gb DDR4 2666mh GPU - 3x Gigabyte R9700, 1x XFX R9700. All cards power limited to 210W. PSU - Seasonic Prime TX-1600W Case - Phanteks Enthoo Pro 2 Server Fans - 3x 140mm at the front, 3x 120mm in the middle, and another 120mm for rear exhaust.
